note: Hand-checked case of px4_navigator: a two-waypoint mission stored in dataman as MAVLink's mission manager stores it, then flown in AUTO_MISSION.  Inputs every tick: the vehicle airborne 10 m above the SITL home (local and global position valid, not landed). Tick 0: vehicle_status (armed, rotary wing, AUTO_LOITER) and home_position. Ticks 2-4: three DM_WRITE requests from client 200 on the mirror port (one each), as MavlinkMissionManager::handle_mission_item / update_active_mission make them (mavlink_mission.cpp:1123-1160, :155-188): item 7 (DM_KEY_WAYPOINTS_OFFBOARD_1, the storage not in use, :972) index 0 and 1, each a 56-byte mission_item_s as parse_mavlink_mission_item makes it from a MISSION_ITEM_INT with frame 3 (GLOBAL_RELATIVE_ALT), command 16 (NAV_WAYPOINT), x/y in 1e-7 degrees, z = 10 m, param4 NaN, autocontinue 1 (:1396-1531): lat = x * 1e-7, altitude 10, altitude_is_relative 1, frame 3, nav_cmd 16, yaw = wrap_2pi(radians(NaN)) = NaN; then item 8 (DM_KEY_MISSION_STATE) index 0, the mission_s state (count 2, storage 7, current_seq 0, land indices -1, mission_id 0x1234). Tick 5: the `mission` topic with the same content. Tick 40: vehicle_status with nav_state AUTO_MISSION (3).  Worked out from dataman.cpp (task_main, _ram_write): each write is answered in its own step with status 0 (STATUS_SUCCESS), the request's client id, type, item and index (ticks 2, 3, 4). Worked out from the navigator: in AUTO_LOITER airborne (tick 0) the triplet is a loiter setpoint (type 2) at the current position, alt = 488 + 10 = 498 (loiter.cpp set_loiter_position). Once the mission runs, the current setpoint is waypoint 0 and the next is waypoint 1, both POSITION (0), lat/lon the stored doubles as binary32 (the ports carry float64 as binary32), alt = home alt 488 + 10 (MissionBlock::get_absolute_altitude_for_item, relative altitude); the previous setpoint is the loiter setpoint it replaces; mission_result: valid, 2 items, current 0, not finished. Observed and explained, not derived: the step at which the mission starts (100). Navigator passes come with its poll: local position at most every 50 ms (orb_set_interval(50), SubscriptionInterval: ticks 0, 1, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100), vehicle_status and mission messages (ticks 0, 5, 40). After the switch at 40 the mission waits for the feasibility check, which needs the geofence loaded from dataman (MissionBase::canRunMissionFeasibility, mission_base.cpp:1451), and for its items in the DatamanCache; both load through asynchronous dataman requests, one round trip per pass, so the mission starts at the third pass after the switch.
